rounds.text: International Conveyors Ltd trades at an extraordinary discount, with a price-to-earnings ratio of just 3.14x compared to a sector benchmark of 21.99x, and an EV/EBITDA of 2.68x against a sector benchmark of 12.26x [E1, E6, E11]. This extreme valuation disconnect occurs despite stellar profitability metrics, including an ROE of 28.05% and a ROCE of 29.59%, both of which vastly outperform their respective sector benchmarks [E9, E10]. Operational momentum is accelerating significantly, highlighted by a trailing twelve-month compounded sales growth of 55%, a TTM profit growth of 126%, and quarterly operating margins expanding to 28% [E17, E21, E31]. Furthermore, intrinsic value models estimate a staggering margin of safety of 92.3%, while a reverse DCF indicates that the current market price absurdly prices in a -19.7% negative earnings growth [E46, E47]. Insider and management alignment is strengthening as promoters have increased their stake to 70.45% alongside a supportive capital goods sector tailwind [E41, E75]. Conceded: the company has delivered a poor sales growth of 4.72% over the past five years and working capital days have increased from 118 days to 173 days [E62, E64].

Despite surface-level cheapness, the business carries severe fundamental strains, highlighted by cash conversion sitting at just 0.51x against reported profit for March 2026, meaning profits are far ahead of cash due to receivables and accruals [E34]. Working capital pressure is compounding this disconnect, with working capital days expanding significantly from 118 days to 173 days [E64]. Furthermore, earnings quality is heavily compromised by a massive other income component of Rs 151 Cr included in earnings [E63]. Balance sheet health is also deteriorating as borrowings spiked to Rs 136 Cr in September 2026, nearly doubling from Rs 73 Cr a year earlier [E39]. Top-line expansion over longer horizons remains weak, reflected in a poor compounded sales growth of 4.72% over the past five years [E62] and flat 3-year compounded sales growth at 0% [E16]. Technical and institutional indicators reinforce these underlying risks, with the stock trading below both its 50-day and 200-day moving averages [E50], a 12-month price return of -19.3% [E52], and institutional money flow registering as negative [E44]. Conceded: [E45]

Conceded: [E63]. However, the bear's alarm over cash conversion [E34] and working capital [E64] is countered by robust absolute cash generation, delivering Rs 35 Cr in operating cash flow and Rs 31 Cr in free cash flow [E35, E36]. The balance sheet remains sound despite higher borrowings [E39], holding a comfortable current ratio of 4.92x and a conservative debt-to-equity ratio of 0.25x [E37, E38]. While longer-term sales growth figures appear muted [E16, E62], momentum has dramatically accelerated with trailing twelve-month sales surging 55% [E17] and quarterly revenue jumping 82% YoY [E66]. The bear relies heavily on lagging technical indicators and negative price momentum [E44, E50, E52], which overlook fundamental outperformance where recent profit growth outpaces soft sentiment by 140% [E57]. Finally, this operational momentum is reinforced by increasing quarterly operating margins [E33] and rising promoter confidence through a higher stake [E41].

Conceded: [E35, E36]. The bull points to robust absolute cash generation of Rs 35 Cr in operating cash flow and Rs 31 Cr in free cash flow, but ignores the warning that cash conversion stands at a low 0.51x because reported profits far outpace actual cash, demanding a close check of receivables and accruals [E34]. The bull cites a comfortable current ratio and conservative debt-to-equity, yet borrowings nearly doubled to Rs 136 Cr in Sep 2026 from Rs 73 Cr a year earlier [E37, E38, E39]. While the bull celebrates surging sales momentum and a 55% TTM increase, it downplays the fact that compounded 3-year sales growth is flat at 0% and 5-year sales growth is a sluggish 4.72% [E16, E17, E62]. The bull dismisses negative price momentum and technical lagging indicators as mere sentiment, but the record shows institutional outflow, negative money flow of -0.63 percentage points, and a weak relative strength rating of 37 against the Nifty 500 [E44, E51, E71]. Finally, the bull glosses over a severe structural deterioration in working capital days, which ballooned from 118 days to 173 days alongside an earnings profile that includes Rs 151 Cr in other income [E63, E64].
